architecture: arm64/pq_a64_common.h:1-40 — a single header, included by all three variants, holds the building blocks shared across variants (predicate setup, exact-sum folds, min/max, bitmap writer, fmix64, group_sum row loop). It emits no code. Variant-specific shared macros sit in pq_a64_neon.h and pq_a64_sve.h, so the include structure has three layers and no duplication between variants.

arm64/pq_a64_neon.h:56-98 + pq_a64_neon.S:46 — the constant tables (bit weights, CMTST constants, the 4 KiB selpos16/selcnt compaction tables) are defined once in the NEON_TABLES macro and emitted once. The compaction tables are generated by the assembler with .rept/.if, so there is no external generator and no hand-written table.

reference-c/pq_dispatch.c:18-64 + pq_a64_common.h:83-93 — each variant is a set of independent global symbols pqk_a64_<variant>_<kernel> (FUNC/ENDF). The dispatcher picks them up through weak references and falls back to the reference for missing ones, so the variants are not coupled to each other or to the dispatcher.

arm64/pq_a64_neon.h:474-480 + pq_a64_neon.S:789 — coupling weakness: filter_i64_bitmap and compare_i64 end with a plain branch into the internal label .Lneon_bitmap_popcount_bytes of another exported function. Their clobber lists and register state therefore depend on another kernel's internals. Many common macros also use fixed registers implicitly (common.h:479-495 MINMAX_RESULT uses x3/x4; 545-568 SBITMAP_PUT uses x2 and x10-x15; 695-722 GSUM_ADD/GSUM_ROWS use x0-x5 and x9-x13), so a 'shared' block only works inside one register-allocation contract.
readability: arm64/pq_a64_scalar.S:43-56, pq_a64_neon.S:54-75, pq_a64_sve.S:52-67 — every kernel has a uniform header block (Args / Result / Clobbers / Registers / Algorithm / Tail) and the same numbered section comments (// -- 1..4), with labels .L<variant>_<kernel>_{main,tail,result,inval}. This consistent skeleton makes the 60 functions easy to navigate.

arm64/pq_a64_common.h:130-156 and 196-214 — comments explain the reasoning: the canonical form pred(x) = ((x-lo) <=u span) ^ inv with its op mapping table, why the op is compared unsigned (negative ints are rejected), and why flipping bit 127 replaces subtracting INT128_MIN. Macro-internal labels consistently use .L<macro>_<step>\@ (common.h:34-35).

arm64/pq_a64_neon.h:154-168 + pq_a64_neon.S:1736-1762 — the non-obvious optimisations (lane forms eq/le/ge/rng, the minmax_i128 hi-word window skip test with adaptive update bursts) come with an explanation of why each is correct, e.g. 'a skipped row cannot change any accumulator'.

Negatives: pq_a64_neon.S is 1998 lines, and minmax_i128 (pq_a64_neon.S:1857-1996, plus 5 helper macros) is a long, dense, heuristic-driven function. Macro arguments mix bare register numbers and full names (common.h:31-33), which the header documents but which is error-prone, e.g. SPRED 12,7,8,9 vs FOLD_SUM64 x4,x5,...
robustness: AAPCS64: no callee-saved register is touched anywhere. A grep of all .S/.h files finds no v8-v15/z8-z15, x19-x29, sp, x30 or x18 operands, and every register range (pq_a64_neon.S:726-739, 940-954, 1663-1664) stays in v0-v7/v16-v31. All kernels are leaves with no frame, and PQ_FILE_END emits .note.GNU-stack (common.h:97-99; scalar.S:796, neon.S:1998, sve.S:873).

Bounds and tails: NEON vector loops run only over whole blocks (e.g. pq_a64_neon.S:106 `and x15, x2, #~31`) and scalar tails read validity bytes that lie exactly within ceil(n/8) (TAIL_VBYTE neon.h:147-152; group_sum GS_ACC_V sentinel bit, neon.S:1170-1186). The 32-byte EMIT8 over-store is argued safe (neon.h:302-304: k <= i, i+8 <= n). SVE stores exactly `count` indices with COMPACT + WHILELO(0,count) + ST1W (sve.S:81-84, 682-685), so there is no over-store at all.

SVE is vector-length agnostic: WHILELO-predicated loops, block loops reset the row counter to the exact block end because INCD can overshoot with non-power-of-two VLs (sve.S:33-35, 169, 786), BITMAP_BLOCKS is VL-independent (sve.h:151-196), and the validity gather is general for any VL (sve.h:28-41).

Overflow and error semantics are exact. sum_i64 uses a 128-bit accumulator and sum_i128 a 192-bit one, and the result checks top == sign(mid) (common.h:409-429). NEON lane growth is bounded by block constants with the reasoning documented (neon.S:223-231, 1619-1622). Invalid ops are rejected before *a/*b are dereferenced (common.h:215-218). NEON group_sum_i64 returns EINVAL with the outputs bit-for-bit unchanged by subtracting the earlier chunks again with wrapping arithmetic (neon.S:1270-1291), and the ngroups == 0 case is handled separately (neon.S:1292-1309).
testability: reference-c/pq_dispatch.c:52-64,104-113 + pq_kernels_internal.h:44-47 — pqk_set_variant / PQ_KERNELS_VARIANT and pqk_variant_table allow any single variant to be selected and its table compared with the reference. The shared randomized differential test (tests/kernel_test.c, 330 lines) uses this for a64_scalar/neon/sve under qemu (Makefile test-cross). This is good for isolating a kernel, but the test is generic: nothing in it is AArch64-specific.

arm64/pq_a64_neon.S:48-52, 1123, 1336, 1763; pq_a64_sve.S:48-50 — the block constants are named and marked 'shrink to exercise the block-flush paths', which helps verification. However, they are plain #define without #ifndef guards, so they cannot be overridden with -D from the build: changing them requires editing a copy of the source.

arm64/README.md:263-306, 855-887 — the guard-page harness, the mutation checks (which needed dedicated data for the minmax_i128 window boundaries), the clobber audit and the shrunken-constant runs are described as throwaway and not committed. The hardest edge cases are therefore not regression-protected in the repository; random data 'almost never reaches the boundary cases'.

No per-kernel unit tests, SVE vector-length test matrix or clobber-audit script is committed under native-kernels/arm64 (README.md:540-543 lists VL 128/384/512/2048 runs done manually). Adding a test means extending the shared C harness.

top_strengths: A disciplined three-layer macro architecture (common / NEON / SVE) with a uniform kernel skeleton and complete per-kernel register/clobber/algorithm headers

Exact and conservative semantics: 128/192-bit exact sums with overflow detected only on the final value, op validation before any dereference, and group_sum EINVAL that leaves the outputs bit-for-bit unchanged (undo pass)
Careful bounds handling: SVE stores exactly the selected count (COMPACT + WHILELO), NEON over-stores are proven to stay within capacity, and validity reads stay within ceil(n/8)
SVE code is truly vector-length agnostic (block-end counter reset, VL-independent bitmap writer, validity gather)
Strict AAPCS64 compliance: leaf functions only, no callee-saved vector or general registers used, .note.GNU-stack in every file
top_weaknesses: Shared macros depend on fixed register contracts and implicit arguments (x2 = n, x3/x4 outputs, x10-x15 bitmap state), and there is a cross-function tail branch into an internal popcount label; both make changes fragile

The verification tools (guard-page harness, mutation tests, clobber audit, SVE VL matrix) are not committed, so boundary cases of the heuristics such as the minmax_i128 skip windows have no regression tests in the repository
Block-size test knobs cannot be overridden from the build (#define without #ifndef)
No BTI landing pads or GNU property note, and no CFI unwind directives: linking into a BTI-enabled binary disables BTI, and profiler/debugger unwinding through the kernels gets no help
Very large single files (pq_a64_neon.S ~2000 lines) with dense micro-optimised kernels such as NEON minmax_i128
suspected_defects: arm64/pq_a64_common.h:83-89 — FUNC emits no `bti c` and the files have no .note.gnu.property section; when linked with -mbranch-protection=standard objects, the whole library and executable lose BTI enforcement (hardening gap, not a functional defect; unverified)

arm64/pq_a64_neon.S:48-52, 1123, 1336, 1763 and pq_a64_sve.S:50 — the block constants are unguarded #define, so -DNEON_SUM64_BLOCK=... on the command line causes a redefinition warning and the file value wins; the testing hook the comments describe cannot be used without editing the source (unverified)

arm64/pq_a64_sve.S:5-7 — the header says 'Validated under qemu-user emulation only (no SVE hardware)', but the repository history records later native ARM runs on SVE2 hardware (commits 572663e, 68a15b9); the documentation in the file looks stale (documentation only)

arm64/pq_a64_sve.S:170 — the comment '< 32 * 2^56: no wrap' misstates the bound (the per-block total of the low halves is at most 2^24 * (2^32-1) < 2^56 whatever the lane count); the code itself is correct (comment accuracy only)

No functional defect found in the traced call paths (filter_i64, group_sum_i64, sum_i128, filter_i128/count_i128, minmax_i128 in scalar/NEON/SVE; PRED_SETUP/PRED128_SETUP checked by hand for all ops including the INT64/INT128 extreme cases)
